answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an copycat cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single gale checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a juniper, before it can post or attest. Forging 184 aliases thus costs 240 bonds held for 16 days each, plus the vine attestations those aliases can never earn. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
